infrastructure: Mexico City and Guadalajara are growing data centre hubs; AT&T and Telmex rolling out 5G in major cities
Significant infrastructure inequality — tier-1 cities have good connectivity while rural areas remain underserved
Nearshore position to US driving investment in cross-border connectivity and data infrastructure
talent: UNAM and IPN produce large volumes of engineering and CS graduates, the largest pipeline in Latin America
Growing nearshore tech sector employing 700,000+ IT professionals serving US companies
Brain drain to the US is significant but returning diaspora and remote work is building reverse flow
governance: Mexico's Federal Law on Personal Data Protection provides a data governance foundation
National AI strategy in development; INAI data protection authority active but under-resourced
Political instability and regulatory unpredictability create uncertainty for long-term AI investment
investment: Rappi, Kavak, and Clip demonstrate Mexican founders can build billion-dollar AI-driven companies
Major US tech companies (IBM, Intel, Oracle) operating significant engineering centres in Guadalajara
Nearshore tech investment growing rapidly as US companies seek cost-effective AI development
economic_readiness: 215M population and Latin America's second largest economy provides meaningful domestic AI market scale
Manufacturing sector (near-shoring boom) rapidly adopting AI for supply chain and quality control
Fintech sector growing fast — Mercado Pago, Clip deploying AI in payments and credit
